hints: Look closely at the shape in P (rolled up) compared to Q (flat and open). Which one is the dry-weather response to hide the stomata in a xerophyte like marram grass?
Remember what makes layer Y (the hinge or bulliform cells) cause rolling. Think about losing water by osmosis, loss of turgor, and what that does to solute concentration and water potential.
walkthrough:
**Observe P and Q**

P shows the leaf rolled into a U-shape with layer Y on the inside. Q shows the leaf flat and open. Rolling up is the classic xerophytic response to dry conditions to trap moist air and reduce transpiration.

**Apply the hinge cell mechanism**

Rolling is caused by cells in layer Y losing water. When they lose water they become flaccid and may plasmolyse, so turgor pressure falls.

Key rule:
$$\Psi = \Psi_s + \Psi_p$$
Loss of water makes solute more concentrated (more negative $\Psi_s$) and lowers $\Psi_p$, so overall water potential $\Psi$ becomes more negative in P.

**Test statements 1 to 4**

Statement 1 is true, cells in P have lost water so have more negative water potential than the turgid cells in Q. Statement 2 is true, more water loss means more plasmolysis in P. Statement 3 is backwards, cells are less turgid in P, not Q. Statement 4 is false, turgid plant cells still have negative water potential, it does not become zero. So only 1 and 2 are correct.

options.A: Includes 1 and 2 which are correct, but also includes 3 which is backwards. Cells are less turgid in P (rolled, dry), not in Q.
options.B: Correct, only 1 and 2 are true. Layer Y cells in P have lost water, so more negative water potential and more plasmolysis than in Q.
options.C: Includes 2 which is true, but 4 is false. Even fully turgid leaf cells in Q still contain solutes, so water potential stays negative and does not become zero.
options.D: Both are false. Statement 3 reverses turgidity (Q cells are more turgid) and statement 4 wrongly claims water potential is zero in Q.
